rationale: Three independently formulated late-layer signals agree on the shape. Step-specific representation structure transfers across datasets at probe accuracy above 0.85, while the correctness predictor built on the same activations falls from 0.87 in distribution to 0.73 on MATH-500, 0.64 on MMLU and 0.60 on the same dataset in a freeform prompt format. A trajectory-geometry classifier needs a per-domain reference set and recovers cross-domain performance only after centroid alignment. A hidden-state norm signal has no universal cutoff at all -- a high norm on GSM8K is a low norm on GPQA -- and replacing its adaptive per-decode threshold with a fixed one collapses AIME24 accuracy from 70.0 to 23.3. The practical rule for the archive: treat any reported AUROC for an internal correctness signal as in-distribution until shown otherwise, and require calibration data per task.
statement: Internal signals that predict answer correctness do not transfer across tasks, even when the structural geometry they are computed from does, so a correctness detector validated on one benchmark says little about another.
